page.description: Proxmox Virtual Environment editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: A Debian-based virtualisation platform combining KVM virtual machines and LXC containers behind one web interface, with clustering, ZFS and Ceph support.
pros: KVM and LXC managed from one web interface.
Clustering, live migration and HA are built in.
Debian base, so the usual Linux tools are available.
Free to install; support and the enterprise repository need a subscription.
cons: Not a desktop: it is a hypervisor appliance.
The enterprise repository needs a subscription; the free one has no vendor support.
The installer offers a beta ZFS setup option with different disk rules.
page.previewNote: No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed for Proxmox Virtual Environment; the page shows the logo only. No image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted.
page.status: Write the ISO to a USB stick and boot the installer; it partitions and erases the target disk and installs the hypervisor. Machines and containers are created afterwards from the web interface.
